claims.text: The baseline AlCoCrFeNiP alloy has limited amorphous-region thickness.
The baseline AlCoCrFeNiP alloy has moderate thermal stability.
Adding 1–2 at.% boron is the proposed effective intervention.
Homogeneous incorporation of 1–2 at.% boron by arc melting and rapid quenching promotes transient P–B clusters.
Boron preferentially binds with phosphorus in this alloy.
Transient P–B clusters sequester phosphorus into locally stable configurations.
The proposed P–B clusters disrupt the atomic packing or network needed for crystallization.
Disruption of regular atomic packing impedes crystalline nucleation and growth.
The proposed cluster-induced disruption increases the nucleation energy barrier for crystalline phases.
Suppressing crystalline nucleation and growth enhances glass-forming ability.
P–B clustering stabilizes the amorphous state thermally.
The boron-added alloy will produce a thicker amorphous region than the boron-free baseline.
The boron-added alloy will have a higher crystallization-onset temperature than the boron-free baseline.
Very rapid cooling can produce an amorphous structure in a phosphorus-containing high-entropy alloy.
The intervention is effective only when boron is uniformly distributed and maintained within 1–2 at.%.
Excessive boron or inadequate mixing can produce stable boride phases.
Formation of stable borides negates the beneficial effect of boron on amorphization and thermal stability.

contradictions.description: The boundary and conditions restrict the hypothesis to samples in which boron remains dissolved and stable borides do not form, but the falsification rule treats extensive boride formation as falsifying the hypothesis rather than as a failure to satisfy those stated applicability conditions.
